# Thesis: balance-sheet COMPOSITION composite. Each item scaled by total assets is a weak, slow characteristic (daily IR .03-.05 alone, turnover ~.03) whose sign held in-sample and out-of-sample (2017-21); combining several weakly related characteristics diversifies their noise, so the composite should carry a higher IR at the same tiny turnover (the IR/sqrt(turnover) route that qualified T_COMP7). Long firms funded by short-term operating liabilities with receivables/inventory-heavy, older (depreciated) asset bases; short goodwill-heavy (acquisitive) and long-term-debt-heavy firms.
# Source: Green, Hand & Zhang, "The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns" (RFS 2017), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhx019; acquisitive firms underperform: Cooper, Gulen & Schill, "Asset Growth and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns" (JF 2008), https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01370.x
# Note: signs were chosen from the first sweep run (field sweep batch 1), so this is partly data-selected; each sign was checked to hold out of sample (OOS1) before inclusion.
# Repair: 5 strongest legs + low-accruals leg (adds an independent slow premium). Parent SWC_BS9 IR .063, TVR .029, corr .477 (< .5), OOS1 .108; needs IR > .07.
# Source (accruals): Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
ta = ts_fill(total_assets)  # total assets, carried forward between reports
cl = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_liabilities)/ta))  # short-term operating liabilities per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ar = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accounts_receivable_excluding_notes)/ta))  # receivables per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
gw = -cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(goodwill)/ta))  # goodwill from acquisitions (short) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ad = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accumulated_depreciation)/ta))  # accumulated depreciation (older asset base) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
oc = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(other_current_assets)/ta))  # other current assets per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
acc = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ta))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(cl) + at_nan2zero(ar) + at_nan2zero(gw) + at_nan2zero(ad) + at_nan2zero(oc) + at_nan2zero(acc))  # equal-weight composite; missing legs count as 0

# Note: signs were chosen from the first sweep run (field sweep batch 1), so this is partly data-selected; each sign was checked to hold out of sample (OOS1) before inclusion.
# Repair: 7 legs (drops inventories and long-term debt, the weakest out of sample). Parent SWC_BS9 IR .063, TVR .029, corr .477 (< .5), OOS1 .108; needs IR > .07.
ta = ts_fill(total_assets)  # total assets, carried forward between reports
cl = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_liabilities)/ta))  # short-term operating liabilities per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
cp = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_portion_of_long_term_debt)/ta))  # debt coming due within a year per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ar = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accounts_receivable_excluding_notes)/ta))  # receivables per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
gw = -cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(goodwill)/ta))  # goodwill from acquisitions (short) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ca = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(current_assets_report)/ta))  # current assets per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
ad = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(accumulated_depreciation)/ta))  # accumulated depreciation (older asset base) per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
oc = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(other_current_assets)/ta))  # other current assets per dollar of assets, ranked and z-scored
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(cl) + at_nan2zero(cp) + at_nan2zero(ar) + at_nan2zero(gw) + at_nan2zero(ca) + at_nan2zero(ad) + at_nan2zero(oc))  # equal-weight composite; missing legs count as 0

# Thesis: High prices that coincide with high volume rank are exhausted. (Alpha #44, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals, to raise IR and cut turnover.
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_044_S Slow IR .067, TVR .786, irtvr .075, corr .602 to #592314 (bar .091).
r = cs_zscore(-ts_corr_binary(high, cs_rank(volume), 5))  # Alpha #44 signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # Alpha #44 + accruals at 1.5x
